1.overview: God creates the heavens and the earth, orders light, sky, land, seas, vegetation, and the lights of the sky across the first four days. He creates sea creatures and birds on the fifth day, then land animals and humanity in God’s image on the sixth, blessing them and giving them food and rule over the earth before declaring all he made very good.

2.overview: God completes creation, rests on the seventh day, and sets it apart. The LORD God forms Adam, places him in Eden with a command concerning the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and makes a woman as his companion.

sections.heading: Creation completed and the seventh day set apart
The LORD God forms Adam and plants Eden
Adam’s work and the command about the tree
The woman is made and brought to Adam

3.overview: The serpent persuades the woman to eat from the forbidden tree, and she gives its fruit to Adam; they recognize their nakedness and hide from the LORD God. After questioning them and pronouncing consequences for the serpent, the woman, and Adam, God clothes the couple and drives them from Eden, guarding the way to the tree of life.

sections.heading: The Serpent and the Forbidden Fruit
God Questions the Man and Woman
Consequences for the Serpent and Humanity

4.overview: Eve bears Cain and Abel, whose offerings receive different responses from the LORD; Cain kills Abel and is sentenced to wander, but the LORD marks him for protection. Cain settles in Nod and his descendants include Lamech and the founders of several crafts, while Adam and Eve have Seth, whose son is Enosh as people begin to call on the LORD.

sections.heading: Cain kills Abel and is judged

5.overview: The chapter traces Adam’s line through Seth, listing each descendant’s age at fatherhood, years lived, and death, while Enoch walks with God and is taken away. Lamech names his son Noah in hope of comfort from the cursed ground, and Noah becomes the father of Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

6.overview: The sons of God take wives from among human women, and the Nephilim and mighty men arise as the LORD sees widespread human wickedness and resolves to blot out life, while Noah finds favor. God identifies Noah as righteous, announces the coming flood, gives him instructions for building the ark and preserving his family and animals, and establishes a covenant with him; Noah does everything commanded.

7.overview: The LORD commands Noah to enter the ark with his family and specified pairs of animals, and Noah obeys as the flood begins. The waters rise over the earth, destroy every living thing on dry land, and prevail for 150 days, while Noah and those with him remain in the ark.

sections.heading: The Flood Begins and the Ark Is Sealed

8.overview: God sends a wind, the floodwaters recede, and Noah tests the ground with birds before leaving the ark with his family and the animals. Noah offers sacrifices, and the LORD declares that he will not again destroy all living creatures by flood and that the earth’s seasons will continue.

9.overview: God blesses Noah and his sons, permits animals as food while forbidding blood, and requires an accounting for human bloodshed. God establishes a covenant never again to destroy all life by flood, marked by the rainbow; Noah’s drunkenness leads to a curse on Canaan and blessings concerning Shem and Japheth, before Noah’s death at 950 years.

10.overview: The chapter lists the descendants of Japheth, Ham, and Shem, tracing their clans, lands, languages, and nations. It records Nimrod’s kingdoms and cities, the borders of Canaan, and the spread of the nations across the earth after the flood.

sections.heading: Descendants of Shem and the Nations

11.overview: The people of Shinar build a city and tower at Babel, but the LORD confuses their language and scatters them across the earth. Shem’s genealogy leads to Terah, whose family includes Abram, Nahor, Haran, and Lot; Terah leaves Ur for Canaan but settles in Haran, where he dies.

12.overview: The LORD calls Abram to leave Haran, promises to make him a great nation and bless all families of the earth through him, and promises Canaan to his offspring. During a famine Abram goes to Egypt, presents Sarai as his sister, and leaves after the LORD afflicts Pharaoh’s household and Pharaoh sends them away.

13.overview: Abram returns from Egypt to Bethel, where conflict between his and Lot’s herdsmen leads them to separate; Lot chooses the Jordan plain and settles near Sodom. The LORD promises Abram the land and numerous offspring, and Abram settles near Hebron and builds an altar.

14.overview: Chedorlaomer and his allied kings defeat the rebellious kings of the Valley of Siddim, capture Lot, and lose their prisoners and plunder when Abram pursues and routs them. Melchizedek blesses Abram and receives a tenth, while Abram refuses the king of Sodom’s goods and allows his allies their share.

15.overview: The LORD promises Abram an heir from his own body and offspring as numerous as the stars, and Abram believes Him. The LORD confirms His land promise through a covenant ceremony, foretelling Abram’s descendants’ enslavement and return before naming the land’s boundaries and peoples.

16.overview: Sarai gives her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abram after years without children; Hagar conceives, despises Sarai, and flees after Sarai mistreats her. The angel of the LORD finds Hagar, directs her to return, and promises many descendants and a son named Ishmael; Hagar names the LORD as the God who sees her, and she bears Ishmael to Abram.

17.overview: God renews the covenant with Abram, renames him Abraham, promises nations and Canaan to his descendants, and commands circumcision as its sign. God renames Sarai Sarah and promises a son, Isaac, as the covenant heir while also promising to bless Ishmael; Abraham circumcises the males of his household.

18.overview: The LORD visits Abraham at Mamre with two other men, announces that Sarah will have a son within a year, and tells Abraham that the outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah has reached him. Abraham questions whether the righteous will be swept away with the wicked and secures the LORD’s agreement to spare Sodom if ten righteous people are found there.

19.overview: Two angels visit Lot in Sodom, where the men of the city threaten them; the angels rescue Lot and his family and announce the city’s destruction. Lot reaches Zoar as the LORD destroys Sodom and Gomorrah, and the chapter ends with Lot’s daughters bearing Moab and Ben-ammi.

sections.heading: Lot and the Men of Sodom
Lot Is Led Out of Sodom

20.overview: Abraham tells Abimelech, king of Gerar, that Sarah is his sister, and God warns Abimelech in a dream that Sarah is married and commands him to restore her. Abimelech confronts Abraham, then returns Sarah with gifts and land, and Abraham prays as God heals Abimelech’s household and restores its fertility.

21.overview: The LORD fulfills his promise to Sarah, and Isaac is born and circumcised; after Sarah demands that Hagar and Ishmael be sent away, God promises to make Ishmael a nation and provides for them in the wilderness. Abraham and Abimelech make a covenant at Beersheba over a well, and Abraham settles in the land of the Philistines.

22.overview: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac at Moriah, but the angel of the LORD stops him and Abraham offers a ram instead. The LORD renews promises of descendants and blessing, Abraham returns to Beersheba, and the chapter lists Nahor’s descendants, including Rebekah.

sections.heading: The LORD’s Promise and Abraham’s Return

23.overview: Sarah dies at age 127 in Hebron, and Abraham mourns her before asking the Hittites for a burial place. Abraham purchases Ephron’s field and cave at Machpelah, and the Hittites deed the property to him before he buries Sarah there.

24.overview: Abraham sends his chief servant to his homeland to find a wife for Isaac, and the servant asks the LORD to guide him to the right woman. Rebekah answers the sign at the well, agrees to leave with the servant, and becomes Isaac’s wife in the Negev.

sections.heading: The Servant’s Account and Rebekah’s Betrothal

25.overview: Abraham’s descendants through Keturah and Ishmael are recorded, and Abraham dies and is buried by Isaac and Ishmael at Machpelah; God blesses Isaac. Rebekah bears Esau and Jacob after Isaac prays, and Jacob obtains Esau’s birthright in exchange for food.

26.overview: During a famine, the LORD renews Abraham’s promises to Isaac, who settles in Gerar and conceals Rebekah’s identity until Abimelech discovers the truth. Isaac prospers, faces disputes with the Philistines over wells, makes a covenant with Abimelech at Beersheba, and Esau’s Hittite wives bring grief to Isaac and Rebekah.

27.overview: Isaac prepares to bless Esau, but Rebekah arranges for Jacob to pose as his brother and bring Isaac food. Isaac gives Jacob the blessing intended for Esau; Esau receives a lesser blessing and plots to kill Jacob, so Rebekah sends Jacob to Laban in Haran and raises her concern about Hittite wives.

sections.heading: Rebekah prepares Jacob to deceive Isaac

28.overview: Isaac blesses Jacob, sends him to Paddan-aram to marry within Rebekah’s family, and repeats the promise of descendants and land; Esau responds by marrying Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael. On the way to Haran, Jacob dreams of a ladder between earth and heaven, receives the LORD’s promises of land, descendants, presence, and return, then names the place Bethel and vows to worship God and give a tenth.

sections.heading: Jacob’s Dream and the LORD’s Promise

29.overview: Jacob arrives near Haran, meets Rachel at a well, and is welcomed by her father Laban, agreeing to serve seven years to marry her. Laban gives Jacob Leah instead of Rachel, then gives him Rachel after another agreement for seven years of service; Leah bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah while Rachel remains barren.

sections.heading: Laban Gives Jacob Leah and Rachel

30.overview: Rachel and Leah compete for children through their servants Bilhah and Zilpah, while Leah bears Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah and Rachel bears Joseph. After Joseph’s birth, Jacob negotiates wages with Laban and uses a selective breeding strategy that leaves him with the stronger flocks and growing wealth.

31.overview: Jacob, urged by God and supported by Rachel and Leah, leaves Laban with his family and possessions; Rachel takes Laban’s household idols, and Laban pursues them to Gilead. After Laban fails to find the idols, Jacob recounts his service and God’s protection, and the two establish a covenant marked by a mound and pillar before Laban returns home.

sections.heading: The search for the idols and Jacob’s defense
The covenant at Gilead and farewell

32.overview: Jacob encounters God’s angels at Mahanaim, learns that Esau is approaching with four hundred men, prays for deliverance, and sends gifts ahead to seek Esau’s favor. At the Jabbok, Jacob wrestles with a man until daybreak, receives the name Israel and a blessing, and names the place Peniel after seeing God face to face; his injured hip becomes the basis for an Israelite food custom.

33.overview: Jacob arranges his family before approaching Esau, and the brothers embrace and weep; Esau accepts Jacob’s gift. Esau returns toward Seir while Jacob travels to Succoth and then Shechem, where he buys land and builds an altar called El-Elohe-Israel.

sections.heading: Separate Journeys to Seir and Succoth

34.overview: Shechem son of Hamor forces himself on Dinah, and Hamor and Shechem seek her marriage while offering intermarriage and settlement to Jacob’s family. Jacob’s sons deceitfully secure the circumcision of the city’s men, then Simeon and Levi kill the males and the other brothers plunder the city; Jacob objects to the danger, and they defend their response to the assault on Dinah.

sections.heading: Simeon and Levi attack the city

35.overview: God directs Jacob to Bethel, where Jacob purifies his household, builds an altar, and receives a renewed name and promises from God. On the journey south Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin, Reuben sleeps with Bilhah, Jacob’s twelve sons are listed, and Esau and Jacob bury Isaac at Hebron.

36.overview: Esau’s wives and sons are named, and he settles in Mount Seir as his household and possessions separate from Jacob. The chapter lists Esau’s descendants and chiefs, the Horite clans of Seir, and the kings who reign in Edom before Israel has a king.

37.overview: Joseph’s favored status and two dreams deepen his brothers’ hatred, and Jacob sends him from Hebron to find them near Shechem and Dothan. His brothers sell him to traders bound for Egypt, deceive Jacob with Joseph’s bloodied robe, and Joseph is sold to Potiphar.

sections.heading: Joseph Sent to Find His Brothers

38.overview: Judah fathers Er, Onan, and Shelah, but the LORD puts Er and Onan to death, and Tamar remains a widow without being given to Shelah. Tamar disguises herself and conceives by Judah; when she reveals his seal, cord, and staff, Judah acknowledges his failure, and she gives birth to the twins Perez and Zerah.

sections.heading: The Birth of Perez and Zerah

39.overview: Joseph prospers in Potiphar’s household, and Potiphar entrusts him with all he owns. After Potiphar’s wife falsely accuses Joseph, Potiphar sends him to prison, where the LORD remains with him and the warden places the prisoners in his care.

40.overview: Pharaoh imprisons his cupbearer and chief baker alongside Joseph, and Joseph interprets their dreams as predicting their outcomes in three days. Pharaoh restores the cupbearer and executes the baker as Joseph foretells, but the cupbearer forgets Joseph.

sections.heading: The Baker’s Dream and Its Fulfillment

41.overview: Pharaoh dreams of seven healthy cows and grain heads consumed by seven lean ones, and Joseph interprets the dreams as seven years of abundance followed by seven years of famine. Pharaoh appoints Joseph to oversee Egypt, Joseph stores grain during the abundant years, and when famine comes he sells grain to Egypt and the surrounding nations.

sections.heading: Pharaoh’s Dreams and the Cupbearer’s Reminder
Joseph Interprets the Dreams and Advises Pharaoh

42.overview: During the famine, Jacob sends ten sons to Egypt for grain but keeps Benjamin at home. Joseph recognizes his brothers, accuses them of spying, demands that they bring Benjamin, detains Simeon, and secretly returns their silver; when they report this to Jacob, he refuses to send Benjamin.

43.overview: As famine persists, Judah persuades Jacob to send Benjamin with his brothers to Egypt, and Jacob sends gifts and double silver with them. Joseph welcomes the brothers, reunites them with Simeon, conceals his identity as he questions them and weeps over Benjamin, then hosts them at a meal where they are seated by age and Benjamin receives five times the portion.

44.overview: Joseph has his silver cup planted in Benjamin’s sack, then sends his steward after the brothers and brings them back to his house when the cup is found. Judah acknowledges that God has exposed their guilt and pleads for Benjamin’s release, offering to remain Joseph’s slave in his place so their father, Jacob, will not die of grief.

45.overview: Joseph reveals himself to his brothers, explains that God sent him ahead to preserve life during the famine, and reconciles with them. Pharaoh offers land and provisions for Jacob’s household, and the brothers return to Canaan with the news, prompting Jacob to go to Egypt.

sections.heading: Joseph Reveals Himself to His Brothers

46.overview: At Beersheba, God tells Jacob not to fear going to Egypt and promises to make his descendants a great nation there, accompany him, and bring him back; Jacob’s family and possessions travel from Canaan to Egypt, and the chapter lists his descendants and totals the family at seventy. In Goshen, Jacob reunites with Joseph, and Joseph instructs his family to tell Pharaoh that they raise livestock so they can settle there.

47.overview: Joseph presents five of his brothers and Jacob to Pharaoh, who grants the family land in Goshen, while Joseph provides for them during the famine. Joseph gathers Egypt’s money, livestock, and land for Pharaoh in exchange for food and establishes a fifth of the harvest as Pharaoh’s share; Israel prospers in Goshen, and Jacob makes Joseph swear to bury him with his fathers.

48.overview: As Jacob lies ill, he recalls God's promise at Luz, claims Ephraim and Manasseh as his own, and recalls Rachel's burial near Ephrath. He blesses the boys with crossed hands, placing Ephraim before Manasseh, and gives Joseph a ridge of land while declaring that God will bring him back to the land of his fathers.

49.overview: Jacob gathers his sons and speaks over them, describing Reuben, Simeon, and Levi’s losses, Judah’s rule, and the distinct fortunes of the remaining tribes, with special blessings for Joseph and a warrior’s image for Benjamin. He instructs his sons to bury him in the cave at Machpelah in Canaan, where his ancestors and Leah are buried, and then dies.

50.overview: Joseph mourns Jacob, leads a large procession to bury him at Machpelah, and returns to Egypt. When his brothers fear his revenge, Joseph reassures them that God turns their evil intent toward preserving lives, and before Joseph dies in Egypt, he makes Israel’s sons swear to carry his bones to the promised land.
